paragraphs: R' Shimon, son of R' Yonah.
Mentioned at the beginning of Bereshit Rabbah, chapter 75; Hyman says the name should read R' Shimon, son of R' Yannai, as the statement appears in Shir HaShirim Rabbah 4:8.[^1][^2]

notes.text: רפע״ה is contextually beginning of parashah 75, not the superseded 175 or Rafa’a readings. פ״ד פ״ח is rendered 4:8 while retaining its source granularity: chapter 4 and a further 8 marker that may label a verse rather than a modern section. No named-edition correspondence is independently checked.

Hyman’s should-read changes the father Yonah to Yannai, retaining his asserted correction force without adopting an identity merger. Both father-title components בר׳/ב״ר remain present as R', rather than being omitted or expanded to Rabbi. All four personal-title components remain R'. Machine בר'ינה/ינאיי differs from the supplied forms and is preserved as provenance.
